knowledgeAnswers.rationale: Section 7.1 and table 8: a swimming pool needs its full volume through the filter no less often than every six hours.
300,000 litres divided by 360 minutes is about 833 L/min, from the standard's six-hour turnover requirement.
Section 7.3: the standard does not recommend cartridge units or diatomaceous earth types for hydrotherapy pools.
The auto-dosing and sensing section says the equipment watches and corrects pH and sanitiser level around the clock, but does not remove the need to test.

practicalCriteria: For a supplied pool and flow reading, calculates the turnover achieved and states whether it meets the limit for the pool type.
Compares an automatic dosing reading with a manual test on a supplied pool, and records any difference.
Isolates and locks out the supply in a supplied scenario before any inspection of pump or controller.
passRule: 80% on knowledge checks; practical sign-off separate
evidenceRequired: Turnover calculation record for the assessed pool
stopWorkCriteria: Electrical fault or exposed live wiring: isolate, do not touch live equipment, and escalate to a licensed electrician.
Achieved turnover below the limit: escalate and keep the pool closed if the operator directs.
Automatic dosing reading disagrees with manual test: stop relying on the controller and escalate.
